clue.text: One with rigid response to game, such as me

definitions.text: One with rigid response to game
definitions.meaning: a gundog that freezes stiffly, pointing, when it scents game birds
the person who composed the crossword, speaking of themself

explanation.surface: A self-description by someone who stiffens at the sight of a game, as the compiler does.
explanation.definitionFit: Setter names both the pointing gundog breed and the compiler of a crossword puzzle.

clue.text: People like you — extremely passionate types, missing nothing

parts.note: so, as in 'so tired', means extremely

indicators.note: missing tells us a letter is dropped from the word for passionate types

parts.note: lovers are people driven by passion
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: The setter addresses the reader, describing ardent people who are lacking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' is a synonym (as in 'so tired'), not a call to take the outer letters of 'passionate'.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter speaks to the reader, who is someone working out crossword clues, a solver.

clue.text: Unifying idea that begins with and ends with 12

parts.note: the answer opens with a pronoun from 12 across: them

indicators.note: and joins the second pronoun so closely to the first that the letter they share is written only once

parts.note: 12 across is PRONOUNS; the answer closes with the pronoun me

explanation.surface: A puzzle-maker defines a unifying idea in terms of its own entry for words like I and you.
explanation.walkthrough: THEM and ME overlap on their shared M: the answer begins with THEM and ends with ME, so one M serves both.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the central subject that ties together a work, here the whole puzzle.

clue.text: Ancient city in European power, second among 12

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: among says the letter for second goes in between the two pronouns

parts.note: 12 across is PRONOUNS: here HE and US

explanation.surface: An old city located within a European power, ranking second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European power' looks like one idea (a nation) but gives two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was a great Greek city on the coast of Asia Minor, now ruins in Turkey.

clue.text: The real me and others reassembled container broken in half

indicators.note: reassembled says the two halves are put back together in a different order
broken in half says the word for container is split into two equal parts

parts.note: a vessel is a container, such as a pot or jar

explanation.surface: Talk of one's true identity, beside a broken pot glued back together.
explanation.walkthrough: VESSEL splits into VES and SEL; swapping the halves gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Selves is the plural of self, a person's true inner identity, so a whole set of them.

clue.text: Station 1 across and down together in school

indicators.note: in places the pronoun for the setter and solver inside the school's name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
1 across is the setter and 1 down the solvers; together they are us

explanation.surface: A railway terminus, linked to two other entries combined at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter (me) plus solvers (you) make US. EUSTON is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is one of the main railway stations in London, serving lines to the north-west.

clue.text: Extremely limited openings for it and others

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the last letter of the word for extremely is lost

parts.note: very means extremely
mouths are openings, as of a river or cave

explanation.surface: Something with very restricted ways in, for it and others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' drops the last letter of VERY. 'it' is short for Italian vermouth, as in the drink gin and it, not the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian, or 'it', is a sweet red vermouth, so it and the others are kinds of fortified wine.

clue.text: Eg best for worst, verbally

parts.note: as verbs, best and worst both mean defeat, so the two opposites mean the same

explanation.surface: It seems to name opposites, best and worst, swapped in speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbally' means as verbs, not spoken: to best someone and to worst someone are both to beat them.
explanation.definitionFit: Words with the same meaning are said to be this; as verbs best and worst are such a pair.

clue.text: Pen music, rondo needing change, sounding wrong

indicators.note: needing change says these letters must be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Writing music in rondo form that needs revising because it sounds wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mispronounced is said incorrectly, so it is spoken wrongly.

clue.text: Odd parts of culture, as this itself is

definitions.text: Odd parts of culture, as this itself is

indicators.note: odd parts are the letters in the first, third, fifth and seventh places of the word

explanation.surface: A clue that describes itself, selected from scraps of culture.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: what you are reading is itself one.
explanation.definitionFit: Every line in the puzzle is a clue, including this self-referential one.

clue.text: Season preceded by 1960s' musical — watch part

indicators.note: preceded by says the musical comes first, ahead of the season

parts.note: Hair is the 1968 rock musical
spring is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A time of year introduced by a hippy-era stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairspring is the fine coiled spring that regulates the balance wheel in a mechanical watch.

clue.text: Ones who cut nested 12

indicators.note: nested says one pronoun sits snugly inside another

parts.note: 12 across is PRONOUNS: two of them are used, one nested within the other
the same cross-reference to PRONOUNS also supplies we, the pronoun that is nested

explanation.surface: People who cut things, set inside one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The single cross-reference supplies both pronouns: one of them sits inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewers chop wood or stone, as in 'hewers of wood and drawers of water'.

clue.text: Formal declarations, excluding 27 words of certain type

indicators.note: excluding signals that the answer to 27 is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: pronouncements are formal declarations
27 across is CEMENT

explanation.surface: Official statements that leave out certain words.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronouns such as I, you and they form a grammatical class, a particular kind of word.

clue.text: Like something that may be first, second or third, without one negative comment

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says the other letters wrap around the one

parts.words: something that may be first, second or third
parts.note: in grammar a person is first, second or third, as with I, you, he
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Describing a thing that ranks first, second or third, minus one critical remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking; a grammatical person is first, second or third.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aspersions is to make damaging remarks, so an aspersion is a disparaging comment.

clue.text: Wrong or right, third person's invested in euros, oddly

indicators.note: invested in says the letters for right and the pronoun go inside, like money put into a fund
oddly says the letters of euros are arranged strangely

parts.note: one, as in 'one does', is a third-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A financial muddle: putting money in euros could be wrong or right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges the letters of euros into EROUS, and 'invested in' places the other pieces inside it. 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous means mistaken or incorrect.

clue.text: Couple, pair of 12, one returned

parts.note: 12 across is PRONOUNS: the pair here is it and me

indicators.note: one returned says the second of the pair of pronouns is written backwards

parts.note: the second of the pair of pronouns from 12 across is me

explanation.surface: Two people together, with one of them coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: The one cross-reference gives a pair of pronouns; only the second is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple in a romantic relationship is called an item.

clue.text: What distinguishes French girlfriend and boyfriend at this point

definitions.text: What distinguishes French girlfriend and boyfriend
definitions.meaning: French amie (girlfriend) differs from ami (boyfriend) only by ..., read as two words
in this place or at this moment

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as HER E: the extra E is hers, the letter that turns ami into amie.
explanation.definitionFit: Here is the adverb for this place or this moment.

clue.text: Awful man with the writer? On the contrary, you and me

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
the writer refers to the setter, so I
no is the reply that contradicts what was just said
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A dialogue: is it a man with the writer? No, it is the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' supplies NO, the word that contradicts, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means shockingly evil or wicked, so dreadful in the strongest sense.

clue.text: Like something of yours or mine that's crazy

definitions.text: Like something of yours or mine
definitions.meaning: yours and mine are possessive pronouns
mad, as if controlled by a spirit

explanation.surface: Describing a belonging of yours or mine that has gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessed means both owned and frenzied as if gripped by a demon.

clue.text: Heterosexual couple hiding half of what's put inside cover

indicators.note: hiding says the pronouns of the couple surround the half-word

parts.note: a woman and a man: she and he

indicators.note: half of takes the second half of the word what

explanation.surface: A straight couple concealing part of what goes into a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the back half of 'what'; 'hiding' puts it inside the couple's pronouns. The definition is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a sword is to slide it into its scabbard, enclosing it in a protective case.

clue.text: He and I each represent one

definitions.text: He and I each represent one

parts.words: He and I each represent one
parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium and I for iodine

explanation.walkthrough: He and I look like pronouns, the theme, but are chemical symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium and iodine are each a chemical element in the periodic table.

clue.text: For example, initially he or she

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: he refers to a male

explanation.surface: Giving an example: at first he, or she.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes F and E from 'For example'; 'he' gives MALE; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the pronoun used for a woman or girl, so it refers to a female.

clue.text: Small pub organised fine party in Ireland

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: organised says these letters are rearranged into order

explanation.surface: A little bar sets up a fine political gathering in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinn Fein is an Irish republican political party active north and south of the border.

clue.text: English 12 — one or the other

parts.note: 12 across is PRONOUNS: here it and her

explanation.surface: In English, a grammatical label meaning one or the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Either means one of two, whichever you choose.

clue.text: Money for church, as 12 after short time

indicators.note: after says the pronouns follow the letter for time

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for time
12 across is PRONOUNS: here it and he

explanation.surface: A church payment, made after only a brief wait.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of income or produce paid to support the church.

clue.text: Like some elements second kind of star made available

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens
lent means made available on loan

explanation.surface: A runner-up star of some sort is offered for use, among the elements.
explanation.definitionFit: A monovalent element has a valency of one, forming a single chemical bond.

clue.text: 2 removing me and then them, for you once

indicators.note: removing says a letter is taken out of the answer to 2

parts.note: 2 down is THEME
the M shared by the pronouns me and them, which overlap in the answer to 2

explanation.surface: Taking oneself and then others away from a unifying idea, for you.
explanation.walkthrough: THEME is built from THEM and ME sharing an M; remove that one M, common to both, to leave THEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the old object form of thou, the archaic singular you.

clue.text: Like beauty pageant participants, for instance, that woman had put outside

indicators.note: put outside says the contraction for that woman had wraps around the short word

parts.note: she'd is short for she had
as, in 'such as', introduces an example

explanation.surface: A beauty contestant, say, was put outside by another woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for instance' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition, though it reads as attached to the contestants.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty contestants traditionally wear a sash across the body naming their region, so are wearing sashes.

clue.text: American's ready, minimally, to embrace Brendan — it's hard stuff

indicators.note: to embrace says the coin wraps around the setter's pronoun

parts.note: ready is cash; the least American cash is a cent
Brendan is the setter, who calls himself me

explanation.surface: The setter claims a firm hug from a ready American, and something hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for cash; a CENT is the smallest US coin. Brendan is the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement sets into a hard building material, binding brick and stone.
